themes_detail.label: Animal Infestation Spike in Homes
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary Animal Private Property complaints surged 700% THIS WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks), signaling a sudden pest or animal control crisis affecting residential properties in Midwood.
evidence: 3 unsanitary animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Spike is statistically significant and marked as high severity
Concentrated in residential area with high density housing stock
reporting_angles: Interview affected residents about what animals/pests are invading homes and whether landlords are responding
Contact NYC Department of Health to determine if there's a documented infestation event or outbreak in the district

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Accumulating
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned Bike complaints jumped 471% THIS WEEK (5 complaints vs. 0.9 weekly average), suggesting a rapid accumulation of derelict bicycles cluttering streets and sidewalks in Midwood.
evidence: 5 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (471% spike, z-score: 3.54)
Spike emerged THIS WEEK, indicating new or worsening condition
reporting_angles: Survey which streets/blocks have the most abandoned bikes and photograph clusters
Contact NYC Parks or NYPD to understand why removal and enforcement has slowed

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Damaged Street Signs spiked 700% LAST WEEK (9 complaints vs. 1.1 weekly average), combined with Dead/Dying Tree complaints up 188% and Overgrown Tree/Branches up 256%, indicating widespread deterioration of outdoor infrastructure in Midwood.
evidence: Street Sign - Damaged: 9 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 average (700% spike, z-score: 4.88)
Overgrown Tree/Branches: 16 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.5 average (256% spike, z-score: 3.43)
Dead/Dying Tree: 9 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.1 average (188% spike, z-score: 3.09)
Three converging infrastructure signals suggest deterioration across public realm
reporting_angles: Document damaged signs (missing, bent, illegible) and assess whether it creates public safety hazards or traffic confusion
Investigate whether NYC Parks has delayed tree maintenance or trimming due to budget cuts or staffing shortages
Interview residents about how overgrown branches affect sidewalk access and street visibility

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Shortage or Overflow
themes_detail.summary: Litter Basket Request complaints surged 380% LAST WEEK (6 complaints vs. 1.2 weekly average), indicating insufficient trash receptacles or overflowing baskets that residents can no longer tolerate in Midwood.
evidence: Litter Basket Requests: 6 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average (380% spike, z-score: 5.73)
Aligns with Unsanitary Condition complaints (994 total over 90 days, #5 complaint type)
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify which blocks or intersections lack adequate trash infrastructure
Contact NYC Sanitation to ask whether litter basket maintenance or deployment has changed recently

themes_detail.label: Boiler/Heating System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Boiler complaints jumped 200% TWO WEEKS AGO (3 complaints vs. 1.0 weekly average), suggesting heating system breakdowns in residential buildings as winter demand peaks.
evidence: Boiler complaints: 3 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.0 weekly average (200% spike, z-score: 4.0)
Heat/Hot Water remains #2 complaint category overall (2,721 complaints over 90 days)
Spike occurred 2 weeks ago; monitor whether it is continuing in current week
reporting_angles: Follow up to confirm whether boiler complaints have persisted THIS WEEK or whether spike has subsided
Interview residents and tenant advocates about unheated apartments and landlord response time
Contact NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development for enforcement data on heat violations in the district
